newsitem.title: UK: New sugar freight orders cited but fixtures scarce.
newsitem.headline: New sugar freight orders cited but fixtures scarce.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a spate of new quoted business at the start of the week but fixtures were relatively scarce, shipbrokers said on Monday.
Firmer business included E D & F Man, reported to be on subjects with its recent Dar es Salaam order for 13,000 tonnes of bulk sugar. No more details were immediately available.
Shipbrokers said Tate & Lyle was very closely working its order for 14/15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maputo to London for mid-December.
Genoc quoted for 13/14,000 tonnes in bags from Poland to Algeria with Egypt and Red Sea options for prompt dates and was thought to have booked a same-sized cargo on the same run.

Czarnikow Rionda was open with two Latin American bagged orders for spot/prompt shipment, 12,000 tonnes from Buenaventura to Red Sea/east Africa and 7,000 tonnes from Santos to east Africa including Madagascar.
Cargill quoted for 11/14,000 tonnes in bulk from Hong Kong or Thailand to south Korea or Indonesia for end December.
David Bruce was in the market with a number of account orders, including 13,000 tonnes from Cuba to Syria for 5/15 January.

Other smaller bagged tonnages were Dunkirk/Hamburg to Lattakia for 9/13 December and a further 2,000 tonnes from the same origin to Aqaba for the same dates. Bruce also quoted for a prompt 3,000-tonne cargo from Santos to Banjul.
Secretan was particularly active on Monday, quoting a wealth of bagged sugar orders with northern Europe and Brazil ports featuring as the most frequent origins.

It was open for 2/4,000 tonnes from Antwerp to Algeria for 5/10 December, 12,000 tonnes from Antwerp/Dunkirk to Algeria for 15/20 December and a further 6,000 tonnes from north France or Antwerp to Alexandria for 8/12 December Secretan also quoted for 14,000 tonnes from north Brazil to Iran for 10/20 December, another 14,000 tonnes from two ports in north Brazil to Lagos for 10/16 December and 3/4,000 tonnes from Santos to Banjul for 10/15 December. Lastly, Secretan was open for a 12,000-tonne bagged cargo from Puerto Quetzal to Colombo for 10/15 January.
Shipbrokers cited a number of account orders for bagged sugar, mainly from Latin American origins.

Allen Chartering quoted a European charterer's order for 12,000 tonnes from Veracruz to west coast Africa for prompt/onwards and Syvers Savoy was also open on account for 7,000 tonnes from Rio to Abidjan for 3/8 December.
Pacmur or nominee was open for 12,600 tonnes from Inchon to Indonesia for 2/10 December and Gyma for 12,000 tonnes from Veracruz to Nouakchott/Cotonou range for prompt/seven days.
